newsitem.title: FRANCE: Chirac hopes for "strong initiatives" on Mideast.
newsitem.headline: Chirac hopes for "strong initiatives" on Mideast.

text.p: French President Jacques Chirac said on Tuesday he hoped for "strong initiatives" from a crisis summit on the Middle East in Washington and urged Israel to respect the existing peace plan.

"A return to calm is vital," Chirac told reporters in the northern town of Arras. "That requires several strong signals...sticking to commitments on Hebron, the closure of the tunnel under holy sites."
"Strong initiatives must also be taken, I hope that they will be in Washington," he said.
In Washington, President Bill Clinton held separate talks with Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and Palestinian President Yasser Arafat at the White House at the start of the summit.

At least 57 Palestinians and 15 Israelis died in five days of clashes sparked last week after Israel opened a tunnel to archaeological sites near Jerusalem's Temple Mount, sacred in Judaism and Islam.

Netanyahu has offered to negotiate a long-delayed Israeli pullback from Hebron, the last and most sensitive of seven occupied West Bank cities, despite an internationally-recognised accord to withdraw.
Chirac said the Middle East peace accords "were what they were, they had the advantage of existing, they must now be respected."
He said he hoped Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak, who has not travelled to Washington, would be able to take an initiative if the U.S. summit did not succeed on all points.
Chirac, who met Netanyahu in Paris last week and urged him to stick to the land-for-peace accords, said he was keeping to plans to visit the Israel and Gaza at the end of the month.
He said he was concerned by a reappearance of "hatred" between Palestinians and Israelis.
Chirac said France "had practically quit the Middle East stage" before he came to power in 1995. He said he had been in contact with all sides during the crisis.
"We are now at a moment when all dangers are possible in terms of confrontation...in terms of a resumption of terrorism," Chirac said.
